output: This section summarizes nonclinical toxicology supporting clinical dosing for naproxen in accordance with ICH M3(R2) and FDA 2005 MRSD guidance. output: This section summarizes the nonclinical toxicology program for glimepiride in accordance with ICH M3(R2) and FDA 2005 MRSD guidance (ICH M3(R2); FDA 2005 MRSD). In a 24‑month mouse carcinogenicity study with dietary administration at 46 and 54 mg/kg/day, pancreatic adenoma incidence was evaluated, and 54 mg/kg/day was the NOAEL in the most sensitive species; using a mouse-to-human body surface area conversion factor of 12, this corresponded to a human-equivalent dose (HED) of 4.5 mg/kg/day and an MRSD of 0.45 mg/kg/day (e.g., 31.5 mg for a 70‑kg adult). output: In accordance with ICH M3(R2), carcinogenicity, genotoxicity, and fertility data for clopidogrel are summarized to contextualize clinical dosing. output: This section summarizes the nonclinical safety program for tamsulosin hydrochloride in accordance with ICH M3(R2) and FDA 2005 MRSD. output: In accordance with ICH S2(R1), a standard genotoxicity battery was conducted for oxycodone, comprising a bacterial reverse mutation (Ames) assay in S. typhimurium and E. coli with and without metabolic activation, an in vitro mouse lymphoma forward mutation assay, two human peripheral blood lymphocyte chromosomal aberration studies at 24 and 48 hours with and without metabolic activation (including evaluation of polyploidy), and an in vivo mouse bone marrow micronucleus assay with systemic exposure confirmed by plasma levels. output: This section summarizes the nonclinical toxicology program in support of first-in-human dose selection in accordance with ICH M3(R2) and FDA 2005 MRSD guidance. output: Nonclinical safety of lanthanum carbonate is supported by a standard package encompassing long-term carcinogenicity in rats (104 weeks) and mice (99 weeks), in vitro and in vivo genotoxicity, and reproductive and developmental studies in rats and rabbits; the highest no-observed-adverse-effect level (NOAEL) for systemic developmental toxicity was 1500 mg/kg/day in the most sensitive species (rabbit).
